oracle: Exact algebraic polynomial identity P(t) - c Q(t) == 0 over Q[t] with degree bound deg <= 2 < N_samples = 5 on positive half-line t = h^2 > 0
expected_behavior: Formal proof audit establishes exact sufficient conditions (PO-1..PO-8) under which symbolic rational-function identity in t = h² > 0 holds globally, and rejects any construction outside the affine-coordinate DAG.

oracle_provenance: Symbolic rational-function degree bound theorem in t = h² (Gram matrix determinant lemma) + 8 machine-checked obligations PO-1..PO-8
theorem_statement: Let K be a single polyhedral solid whose affine chart has base coordinates in R^2 independent of height h > 0 and vertical axis e_3 with metric Gram matrix G(t) = G_base (+) diag(t) where t = h^2 > 0. If every point/line/plane in the construction DAG is formed solely by affine operations (solid vertices, midpoint, divide_segment with constant ratio, centroid, line/plane intersection, parallel line/plane) or metric projection onto the base plane (z=0), then every point coordinate vector in the chart is independent of t. Consequently, every inner product u^T G(t) v is an affine polynomial in t of degree <= 1, every Gram determinant is affine in t of degree <= 1 (by the matrix determinant lemma since G(t) - G(0) has rank 1), and each whitelisted goal squared g(t)^2 = P(t)/Q(t) has polynomial numerator/denominator degrees (deg P, deg Q) <= (2, 2). Therefore P(t) - c Q(t) == 0 over Q[t] (and agrees at N = 5 witness points t in {1, 4, 9, 25, 49}, 5 > 2) with Q(t) > 0 for all t > 0 implies g(t)^2 = c identically for all h > 0.
